Sports.title: Unlucky or unfair? Did Mercedes strategy cost Russell Monza win?
Sports.content:
George Russell feels Mercedes were correct to split strategies despite losing out to Kimi Antonelli in a thrilling Italian Grand Prix.

Russell led Antonelli, who stormed through the field from 19th to be in the lead battle after just 13 laps, by one second when a race-changing Virtual Safety Car was called with 25 laps remaining.

Mercedes pitted Antonelli, but not Russell, for new medium tyres, which put the team-mates 15 seconds apart when the VSC ended.

From sixth, Antonelli overtook his rivals one by one then caught and overtook Russell with three laps to go to win his home event.

It leaves Russell 66 points behind Antonelli in the Drivers' Championship with 10 rounds to go.

"I was on the hard tyre and Kimi was on the medium tyre [when the VSC came], so if either of us were to pit, it was going to be Kimi," said Russell.

"I guess, why I was just a little bit annoyed with the timing of that VSC because, like Max said, I think it would have been tough for those guys on the medium to have competed with anybody on the hard tyre. But, it takes nothing away from Kimi's drive altogether."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The crowd erupted with boos aimed at George Russell as he stepped on Monza podium

Had Mercedes pitted both drivers, Antonelli would have been stuck behind for a few seconds in the pit lane, therefore losing track position to Max Verstappen, who also pitted under the VSC.

Russell told Sky Sports F1: "The VSC came at an awkward time. I don't think the team knew what the right strategy was and, as Max was in the fight, decided to split the strategy which was probably the right thing for the team to do.

"In hindsight of course, it's easy to say I should have pitted or, if I won the race, they would have said Kimi should have stayed out.

"I would have liked to have had a fight with Kimi. It was quite a nice battle and I felt I was holding my own at that point. That was probably another reason the team wanted us to go on a different strategy. I get it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli and George Russell go wheel-to-wheel for the Italian Grand Prix several times

Schiff: I don't know why Russell is not more frustrated Sky Sports F1's Naomi Schiff



"I don’t know why he’s not a little bit more frustrated, if I’m totally honest.



"I guess if you’ve given it all and you think that have actually executed the best strategy, and your team-mate has beaten you outright from P19 on the grid, then maybe there is nothing to be frustrated about, other than the fact that Kimi is going to be incredibly tough to beat this season."

Wolff explains Mercedes' thinking at time of VSC

Toto Wolff revealed Mercedes' computer systems told them, at the time of the VSC, that Russell's strategy would be faster than Antonelli's with the Italian expected to "come close but wouldn't catch".

Mercedes believed the hard tyre was a "forever tyre" that would effectively last the whole race, but not with the performance of the medium.

"The differentiator today was the ability going through the traffic [from Antonelli]. We've seen it with other great ones in the past. Lewis [Hamilton] put it in some of the races and that's what he's shown today," said Wolff.

"There's just no stopping when a driver and a car are one, then there's nothing that can stop them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell explains why the team chose not to pit him during the VSC, which potentially could have cost him the win in Monza

Coming into the weekend, Antonelli was expected to lose points to his closest title rivals - Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris.

Instead, he's extended his advantage and Russell is set to start at the back himself in one of the upcoming races as he does not have enough engines to finish the season without a grid penalty.

However, Russell says he's "not thinking about" the title race and instead is looking at the positives of being competitive in Monza and Zandvoort compared to the events before the summer break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli reflects on his sensational 19th to first Monza victory, catching teammate George Russell to claim a landmark home win and strengthen his championship lead

"We are where we are. Kimi's been driving incredibly this season and deserves to be leading the championship and he's got a healthy lead," he said.

"I'm not going to think about the fight or the comeback. I'm just thinking about going to every race and trying to win it. It will be what it will be. I'm not putting any pressure on myself in this regard, saying 'I need to do this or that'. I just need to win more races and, of course, he's in this spot."

Sports.title: No blockbuster signing but Arsenal's attack still finding another level
Sports.content:
Midway through the second half at the Emirates Stadium, Martin Odegaard picked up the ball in an inside-right position and threaded a pass towards Kai Havertz, whose flick allowed the onrushing Bukayo Saka to test Emiliano Martinez.

The Chelsea goalkeeper managed to push his effort around the post. But the slick passage of play was one of many examples of how the champions, on maximum points after a third straight win, are feeling the benefits of having the trio available again.

Much of the focus ahead of the game had fallen on Chelsea's front three. How would Arsenal contain Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer? It seemed the script had been written when Rogers stunned the ground into silence after 77 seconds.

But Arsenal regained their poise and proved a point about their own attack. Rogers was one of three high-profile forwards to elude them during the summer along with Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez. But they may still have the tools to level up without them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Arsenal's 2-1 win over Chelsea

The key is simply to get their best attackers on the pitch, something injuries prevented for much of the last two seasons. This was the first time since December 2024 that Odegaard, Havertz and Saka have started a third straight league game together.

Odegaard and Havertz made the decisive contributions, combining for the winner when the former finished coolly following the latter's dummy. Earlier, Havertz had equalised with his precise finish at Martinez's near post from the edge of the box.

"They have been Arsenal's two best players," said Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville when they were substituted to loud applause. Saka wasn't bad either, tearing into Chelsea on the right and earning a standing ovation of his own later in the second half.

The clamour for Arsenal to add a forward was of course understandable. The club's efforts, although ultimately fruitless, showed they appreciate the need for it. In an ideal world they would have marquee attacking signing leading them into this season.

Image: Martin Odegaard celebrates after scoring Arsenal's second goal

But they can go at least some way to making up the shortfall by keeping Odegaard, Havertz and Saka fit. The last time they managed it over the course of a full season, in 2023/24, they finished the campaign with a club-record 91 Premier League goals.

It helps that Odegaard has rediscovered his scoring touch.

Their captain is unrecognisable from the player who only scored once in 36 games last term. His winner puts him on three in four for the new campaign; his latest another example, following a nearly-identical goal in the Community Shield, of how he is getting into the box more. Arteta noted other differences.

"He's fit, and confidence-wise I think it's one of the highest that I've seen him," he said. "He also has a point to prove from last season after missing so much football, and Bukayo the same. We missed so many attacking players last season for long, long periods."

His chemistry with both Saka and Havertz is another factor. They were the two players he passed to most against Chelsea. Odegaard found Saka 10 times and Havertz seven. But his understanding with both, the latter in particular, extends to off-the-ball runs too.

"He's a really smart player and moves so well," Odegaard told Sky Sports of Havertz. "He takes defenders' attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind, I'm always free."

Arteta agreed. "When you start to feel the chemistry they have between them and what they can produce, it's great," he added. "For me, he gets to that point because he's enjoying his football.

Image: Arsenal's Kai Havertz celebrates his goal against Chelsea

"And when you are there, you have to enjoy what you do, you have to play with real intent, and that's what I loved to see from him today. He was running forward, he took shots, he created so many situations for his team-mates, so it was great."

Havertz, also on three goals in four games, has been similarly impactful. This was another all-round performance to underline just how much he gives the side, as an aerial outlet and runner in behind who links with his midfielders and works incessantly.

"To displace Havertz from this team, you need to be one of the best players in the world," said Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

Three Premier League games in, Odegaard, Havertz and Saka account for all six of Arsenal's goals. But the performance against Chelsea showed it has been a collective endeavour too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers clashed during the game

As against Coventry and Aston Villa, Arsenal appeared notably more fluid in the final third, with Havertz often pulling to the right, Saka popping up centrally or even swapping flanks with Christos Tzolis, and Riccardo Calafiori appearing everywhere.

"It was another layer," added Arteta to Sky Sports. "Another layer of dynamism, of threat, of intent, of aggression in the attacking phase. You have certainly seen that today."

Chelsea struggled to cope with the level of movement. Even before the second goal, Arsenal had got in behind their backline repeatedly, their combinations, usually in the right half-space, where Odegaard and Saka, in particular, do their best work, proving problematic.

The challenge now is to keep them fit. A spate of injuries like those suffered in the last two seasons might leave fans pining for that blockbuster signing again. But for now they can enjoy what they have. Odegaard, Havertz and Saka are leading their charge.

Sports.title: Defending champs Alcaraz and Sabalenka reach US Open quarter-finals
Sports.content:
Clinical Carlos Alcaraz moved a step closer to making more tennis history after cruising into the US Open quarter-finals.

The Spaniard, still showing no signs of the wrist injury that sidelined him for more than four months before the tournament, dismantled American Tommy Paul in straight sets.

Alcaraz is already the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam and should he go on to win back-to-back Flushing Meadows crowns, he would become the only man in the Open Era to successfully defend major titles on all three surfaces.

Having won on the grass of Wimbledon in 2023 and 2024 and on the French Open clay in 2024 and last year, the 23-year-old can complete the set on hard courts if he triumphs next Sunday.

Paul, the 20th seed, had talked up his chances before the match, saying "I like to think of myself as somebody who always thinks I can beat those (top) players".

But a 6-4 6-3 6-4 defeat means Alcaraz has now beaten the 29-year-old six times in a row, winning the last 14 sets they have contested.

He actually faced two set points at the end of the third, but swatted them away with two contemptuous forehand winners on his way to victory in two hours and 21 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tommy Paul pulls off a sensational point against Carlos Alcaraz with a remarkable 100mph shot around the net

'I think I'm back to full power' - Alcaraz issues US Open warning

"I played my game. I tried to put my style on today's match.

"Tommy is such a talented player and his shots are dangerous and hard to control, so I just tried to be ready for the battle, ready to run if it mattered.

"I tried to be aggressive all the time and tried not to let him stay on the court. I put so much pressure on the return game. It helped a lot to play relaxed, calm and to think clearly.

"I'm really happy with the performance today. Am I back to full power? I think so. I play well every time I come here, and I just try to enjoy it.

"It doesn't matter I was out for four-and-a-half months; every time I come here I play my best."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A wayward ball lands in a spectator's honey deuce cocktail, but the fan sees the funny side and laughs off the mishap

Alcaraz 'different class' and 'in another stratosphere'

Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman:

"It's a pleasure to watch Alcaraz go through the gears. He's just got better and better as this tournament has gone on.

"Tommy Paul gave it everything he had but, at the end of the day, Alcaraz was different class.

"The forehand was firing. I've seen plenty of good forehands over the years, but I think Alcaraz's might be the best. It's unbelievable how he hits it so hard and doesn't look like missing."

Image: No player in US Open history has a higher win percentage than Carlos Alcaraz

Sky Sports Tennis' Martina Navratilova:

"It's really crazy he got this good this fast. Normally, when people have that many options to their game, it takes a while to figure out how to play the game. But not Carlos, he's just in another stratosphere."

Sabalenka edges Townsend to reach last eight

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open Round 16 match between Aryna Sabalenka and Taylor Townsend

Aryna Sabalenka clung onto her US Open title and the world No 1 spot after an unconvincing win over Taylor Townsend.

The Belarusian battled through 6-4 6-3 on Arthur Ashe Stadium in a bizarre match which featured 11 breaks of serve from 19 games.

Sabalenka has spent 99 weeks at the top of the rankings but she needs to win a third straight Flushing Meadows title - and for current No 2 Elena Rybakina to lose before the semi-finals - if she is to reach a century.

"It's super challenging but once again it's important to focus on yourself," said Sabalenka, who had to come from a breakdown in the second set against popular American Townsend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Taylor Townsend and Naomi Osaka both made a statement with their eye-catching outfits as they took to the court. But who wore it best? You decide...

"I was like 'okay, you are down the break, just try to return the serve and put as much pressure on her as possible'.

"I was just trying to stay focused on myself, not only point by point but ball by ball. I'm happy I was able to turn around the second set, I think it was a key moment."

In the quarter-finals Sabalenka will play Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, after the Czech came through a titanic battle against Marta Kostyuk in a repeat of their semi-final at SW19.

Ukrainian Kostyuk saved five match points, two at the end of the second set and three in the decider, before Noskova eventually got over the line 7-5 5-7 6-4.

How did Sabalenka perform?

Sky Sports Tennis' Martina Navratilova:

"It was good enough. It was pretty solid. Townsend had more winners but Aryna did really well returning serve and with passing shots.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A rare sight from Aryna Sabalenka as she completely misses two returns from Taylor Townsend's serve, failing to make contact with the ball on either occasion

"Townsend tried to come into the net more, but she wasn't successful there, that's how well Sabalenka played from the baseline.

"Overall, I would give Sabalenka a 'B' because she lost her serve so many times, but she played really well when it mattered."

'Showwoman Sabalenka meant business'

Sky Sports Tennis' Annabel Croft:

"There was a lot of ferocious intensity to what Sabalenka brought onto this court. When she went a break down in the second set, she really galvanised herself. When she got back on track, she let out the most enormous shriek and you just knew she meant business.

"The passion, the aura, the mentality, the personality, she brings so much to every court. She's a great showwoman and puts on a show whenever she plays tennis. She understands this isn't just sport, it's entertainment as well.

"She is going to take some beating. She doesn't look as vulnerable as I was expecting. So far, she hasn't dropped a set and looks in very good shape."

Sports.title: Ødegaard fires winner as Arsenal complete comeback win over Chelsea
Sports.content:
The first heavyweight encounter of the Premier League season was previewed in some quarters as the immovable object versus the irresistible force. Arsenal do not give an inch. Chelsea have been fun and free-scoring under Xabi Alonso. Yet that overlooked something pretty fundamental. The percussive force of Arsenal’s game when they have the ball and want to make something happen.

Chelsea landed a significant blow after 77 seconds when Morgan ­Rogers put them in front with a nicely executed volley from the edge of the area. It was not only the first goal that Arsenal have conceded this season but one with rich narrative strands. Rogers was chased by Arsenal over the summer only to join Chelsea for £117m.

The story here was about Arsenal’s reaction. The sheer fury of it. For a blistering spell that culminated in Kai Havertz’s equaliser on 25 minutes, they threatened to blow Chelsea off the pitch. Arsenal’s confidence shone through. They had not lost to their cross-town rivals in 11 previous ­meetings in all competitions, winning eight, but it was rooted in more than that. They had too much for Chelsea and they knew it.

Martin Ødegaard’s goal shortly after half-time proved the dif­ference – after a stunning feint by Havertz – and it continued Arsenal’s perfect start to their title defence. It is now three wins out of three. They will take some stopping. Then again, everybody already knows this.

It was possible to feel a blast from the past as Alonso lined up with three central defenders. Almost exactly 10 years ago, Antonio Conte brought Chelsea here and trailed 3-0 at half‑time. Cue the manager’s switch to three at the back, a click and a bolt towards the title. This was the acid test for Alonso and his team could not have made a better start. They had scored very early in the Spaniard’s first two league matches against Fulham and Brighton and it was the same again.

Arsenal offered £80m to Aston Villa for Rogers but no more. ­Chelsea went much higher and there was an inevitability about him ­showing up when it mattered. Arsenal did not clear their lines after a Reece James free-kick and when Jorrel Hato outjumped Ødegaard, the ball broke nicely for Rogers. The volley was threaded into the bottom corner. Could David Raya have done better? It felt that way in the moment.

Arsenal’s response was ferocious. It was the intensity and the physical levels. The Emirates sounded like a bear pit as the home crowd yelled after what felt like every coming together, every time an Arsenal player tumbled over. The equaliser was extensively trailed and it came when Havertz was allowed to drift along the edge of the Chelsea area from right to left. There was no challenge and his low left-foot shot beat ­Emiliano Martínez inside the near post.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers is challenged by his former Aston Villa teammate Ezri Konsa. Photograph: Daniel Hambury/EPA

It was a soft concession and out of keeping with the resilience that ­Chelsea had shown up to that point. Especially Martínez. The former ­Arsenal goalkeeper had thrown himself into a thicket of legs to keep out a low Ødegaard free-kick delivery, taking a boot to the head from Gabriel Magalhães for his ­troubles. He also saved brilliantly from the Arsenal ­centre-half shortly ­afterwards, ­keeping him out at close quarters after João Pedro had failed to clear a Declan Rice free-kick. On the rebound, Ezri Konsa hit the post before Riccardo Calafiori lashed the loose ball home. The goal check showed Konsa was offside and it was disallowed.

Arsenal created a staggering number of openings before the Havertz goal. Chelsea put their bodies on the line. Martínez got his angles right to deny Bukayo Saka; Wesley Fofana made a big block to thwart Havertz. After James had worked Raya from distance, Arsenal stormed to the other end and Hato leapt into a ­saving block on Ødegaard.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It was breathless stuff and it was as if Arsenal exhaled after the ­equaliser. This kind of tempo was surely unsustainable. Chelsea kicked out a foothold. Rogers curled past the far post and there was the crucial moment just before the interval when João Pedro got Pedro Neto away up the right. He cut inside and steered a low shot against the far post.

Arsenal cleared their heads for the second half and they were in front almost immediately. ­Ødegaard started and finished the move but it was all about the dummy from Havertz, who knew where his captain was when Christos Tzolis sent over a low ball from the left. Havertz’s move froze Fofana and Ødegaard had the freedom of the Chelsea area to ­finish. A couple of words about ­Tzolis: very polished.

Arsenal were not afraid to go long and fast from back to front through Raya; the challenges were numerous for Chelsea. They looked to their big guns to mount the fightback. Rogers almost got away only to be halted by a thunderous Konsa slide challenge. Cole Palmer flitted around the edges. He had a couple of half chances.

Saka forced Martínez into a fine save after a lovely touch from Havertz and Arsenal almost scored again from a corner, Martínez grabbing a loose ball when he was already on the ground. Chelsea pushed in the closing stages and they could point to the moment on 89 minutes when Estêvão, on as a substitute, sent a drive searing from the edge of the area and watched Raya tip over. Arsenal did not deserve to drop points.

Sports.title: ‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United draw
Sports.content:
David Moyes praised Everton’s resilient response to a troubled week after his side twice came from behind to salvage a point against Manchester United through Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s long-range strike.

The deadline-day signing, who was introduced in the 77th minute after James Garner pulled up with cramp, preserved Everton’s unbeaten start to the season with a 25-yard effort in the 96th minute.

Tyrique George also scored a superb equaliser to lift the mood at Hill Dickinson Stadium after transfer deadline day had left Moyes with a weaker squad and only one striker in Thierno Barry.

The Everton manager insisted it had been easy to keep the negativity away from his players. “It was the exact opposite,” he said of the potential negative impact on his squad.

“I said to the players there would be no excuses from any of us and the players all agreed. The players hugely bought into it. It can hurt you being a player down but it can also have the opposite reaction.

“Sometimes when you have less players it means everybody has to be ready and you have to find a way of making it work. Who knows how it will go? It will be difficult when we have three games a week.”

Moyes also paid tribute to the quality of the goals from Maitland-Niles and George, who cancelled out finishes from Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko respectively.

“If nobody knew you that goal would get you plenty of headlines,” he said of Maitland-Niles, a £4.3m deadline-day signing from Lyon. “It was a brilliant goal, brilliant technique. We have not had a chance to get to know Ainsley but it was a great start from him.”

Sports.title: Embattled Fifa president Infantino declares intention to stand for re-election
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has reiterated his desire to stand for re-election next year despite the continuing controversy surrounding his leadership.

Infantino refused to answer questions about his future when asked by reporters at the Women’s Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday. The 56-year-old Swiss is under severe pressure to resign after trying to sell stakes in Fifa tournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors.

Uefa, the European governing body, has led calls for Infantino to step down with further opposition coming from the Asian confederation and Concacaf, which represents countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.

But for the first time since the plan became public, Fifa has reiterated Infantino’s intention to run for a fourth and final term in next year’s elections. Should he be re-elected, he will continue to serve as head of world football until 2031.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino. Montagliani, a Fifa vice-president, had long been regarded as a close ally of Infantino, but there were signs, even before he distanced himself over the now-scrapped plan to allow private investment into World Cups, that he viewed Fifa’s purpose somewhat differently to the Swiss.

However, Infantino is not without friends – Saudi Arabia, the 2034 men’s World Cup hosts, came out in support last month, with African football’s governing body, Caf, and South America’s Conmebol also supportive.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

As the only declared candidate so far for the election due to take place in March 2027, Infantino will need a simple majority of votes from the 211 federations affiliated to Fifa to extend his term of office, which began in 2016. Candidate nominations for next year’s election must be submitted by 18 November.

Sports.title: Armstrong spurns golden chance to win derby as Birmingham and Wolves draw
Sports.content:
If only Adam Armstrong, the Wolves striker presented with a golden chance in the 87th minute, had shot into the same corner of the net at the Railway End that his teammate ­Jackson Tchatchoua had located when scoring one of the most ­memorable own goals at the end of the first half, then César Peixoto’s team would surely now be second in the Championship.

Instead Armstrong, one of the Football League’s most proven goalscorers, lifted his shot over an open goal from 10 yards when played in by Fer López at the end of this implausibly open derby. Birmingham ultimately deserved to extend their unbeaten start to the league season.

After their 4-2 defeat at West Ham on Tuesday, Wolves look as vulnerable defensively as they can be devas­tating going forward. Only Burnley, relegated with them last season, have conceded more than their 10 goals.

Tom Wagner, the ­Birmingham chair, was back in the St Andrew’s directors’ box for the first time since a stroke in February and was treated to a thrilling game. Spoils were shared but Chris Davies was happy with his side after they twice came from behind. “I’ll always be content when the players put in that heart and spirit,” the ­Birmingham manager said. “When you look at the quality of their team, I’ll be astonished if they’re not in the top four. Second half, we put them to the sword.”

López scored in the third ­minute for Wolves and, after Jay ­Stansfield equalised in controversial circum­stances, Ladislav Krejci gave the visitors the lead again. But then came the moment that could haunt ­Tchatchoua. The Cameroon right‑back was under no pressure as he went to turn a long diagonal from Phil Neumann back towards his ­goalkeeper – but instead looped the ball wide and over José Sá into his own goal.

That moment set the tempo for the rest of a game. Wolves, despite ­retaining the majority of their ­Premier League squad after the transfer deadline, know sheer quality of player alone will not mean promotion.

View image in fullscreen Adam Armstrong (left) reacts to his missed chance to win it for Wolves at Birmingham. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Peixoto called for video assistant referees to be brought in to the Championship after Stansfield appeared to handle when bringing down Patrick Roberts’s brilliant chip before hammering home Birmingham’s first equaliser. “If the referee doesn’t see it, then what can you do?” Stansfield said.

Peixoto said: “I don’t know why they don’t have VAR in the Champion­ship. It’s very important to help the refe­rees to take the best decisions. I saw a handball and in the screen we saw a handball.” The ­Portuguese coach also confirmed that in a pre‑season meeting with Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL), ­managers were told that grappling at corners would be penalised. “But it’s not happening,” he said.

While the home side dominated the second half, Wolves could have put the game to bed before Birmingham got going. López was involved in the buildup before advancing to side‑foot home Rodrigo Gomes’s right‑wing cross to the near post for his third goal of the season.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Then in the 19th minute, ­Christoph Klarer’s poor touch invited Raúl ­Jiménez to steal the ball and put in Gomes who allowed James ­Beadle to save his dinked attempt.

Krejci is one of the elite players surprisingly still at Wolves. The Czechia captain’s bullet header, after André flicked on Hugo Bueno’s corner, gave Wolves another endorphin boost. It was short-lived, however, as Tchatchoua lobbed home his tragicomic own goal. Jiménez hit the crossbar, as he did in defeat at West Ham, but then Neumann headed against the same woodwork midway through the second half.

Wolves had the clearest of many chances both teams had to win the game. López dispossessed Demarai Gray inside the area and, faced with the goalkeeper, squared for ­Armstrong. Somehow he contrived to lift the ball over the empty goal. “The way Jack[son Tchatchoua] committed his mistake, Adam committed the mistake in the opposite side,” Peixoto said. “We have to take the confidence to them and keep fighting and work hard for the next game.”

There was still time for ­Birmingham to think they had won it as Marvin Ducksch arced a free-kick towards the top corner. There, however, was Sá to show why he was awarded a new contract, as he tipped the ball aside to ensure this pulsating match finished even.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League: Shaw doubles up to give Manchester City winning start
Sports.content:
Some things just feel inevitable. Some strikers just feel inevitable. Despite a new season, a fresh start and new opponents, it is still the same storyline for Manchester City: Khadija Shaw wins them the game. The Jamaica striker began the campaign exactly how she finished the previous league season, with two goals, and demonstrated why it was so crucial that the club eventually persuaded her to sign a new contract in the summer.

Last season’s Golden Boot winner in the Women’s Super League could have scored at least twice in the first half had it not been for an excellent debut performance from Sophie Baggaley in goal for promoted Birmingham.

Shaw, though, was not to be denied and she rose highest to head in twice from second-half corners, taken first by Kerstin Casparij and then by the debutant Beth Mead, to score her side’s second and third goals in a 3-1 victory. By then, Mary Fowler’s low finish had already opened the scoring with Manchester City’s 1,000th goal as a professional women’s side.

Birmingham grabbed a late consolation goal through Océane Hurtré, who capitalised on a defensive lapse from Jade Rose and rolled the ball home in the 90th minute, and there were plenty of encouraging signs overall for the second-tier champions of last season.

Quick Guide Palace face scrutiny over substitutions Show Crystal Palace could face a points deduction or potentially be forced to replay their game against Everton on Sunday, which Palace won 1-0, after it emerged that the hosts breached the rules around substitutions by making changes at four separate moments in the second half of the Women's Super League match. The WSL, Pro Ref and both clubs have all launched investigations into the incident. The newly promoted Palace brought on Kirsty Howat to replace Shannon O'Brien in the 97th minute, having already made three previous substitutions across three separate second-half opportunities. A WSL spokesperson said: "We can confirm there was a breach of competition rules in the Crystal Palace versus Everton match. Crystal Palace used a fourth substitution opportunity during a fourth stoppage in play, when the rules permit a maximum of three substitution opportunities per match. We will now conduct an investigation alongside both clubs and Pro Ref and update in due course." Jo Potter's side were already leading the match thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith's 34th-minute opener. There were eight minutes of stoppage time indicated for the end of the second half, so the substitution in question came with merely seconds remaining. The consequences could be significant for Palace, depending on the outcome of the investigation and the verdict of any potential tribunal. The WSL's rules regarding the fielding of an ineligible player list the potential punishments in rule 7.13.2, which include the possibility that the points gained from the match be deducted or that the match be replayed. It is understood that the team of match officials who worked on that Palace-Everton game will not be appointed to the next round of games in WSL/ WSL2 on the weekend of 12-13 September, in light of this incident. Teams are permitted to use no more than three substitution opportunities per match, in addition to being able to make replacements at half-time and for concussion substitutions. Tom Garry Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The Blues were playing on the same ground where they were relegated in 2022 after a 6-0 loss to City, but on Sunday Amy Merricks’s side look far more competitive than the Birmingham team that said goodbye to the top tier four seasons ago, having kept the scoreline goalless until after half-time.

Nonetheless, on the day of Lauren Hemp’s 200th City appearance it was a dominant start from the defending champions, whose head coach, Andrée Jeglertz, said: “We created a lot of scoring chances. The first half [we were] a little bit hesitant on the ball, not determined with or without the ball, but the second half was better.”

View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s Lisa Baum fires in the only goal at Brighton. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

Merricks, who hailed Baggaley’s debut as “exceptional”, said: “We got into some good areas and lacked just a bit of anticipation that we would get there. That’s just down to belief, that’s not quality. I’m really pleased with the performance. I’m disappointed with the result but really pleased with the platform we’ve given ourselves to build on.”

Earlier, Lisa Baum marked her Arsenal debut with an exquisitely taken goal and her early strike was enough to secure a 1-0 victory at Brighton and inflict a defeat on their new head coach, Arturo Ruiz. The 19‑year‑old Germany youth international created room to shoot inside the area in the 10th minute and rifled home a clinical finish from a tight angle, in off the underside of the crossbar, to make an immediate impression on the delighted, travelling Arsenal fans behind that goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Baum, who arrived this summer from RB Leipzig, was one of four new signings to start the game for Arsenal, alongside Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez. Arsenal had failed to win at Brighton in the past two league campaigns and will have been very satisfied to open their title bid with a victory as they seek to hunt down a first league title since 2019. Ruiz, who has been in charge at Brighton for nine days, saw some encouraging signs from his new team with Kiko Seike and Fran Kirby both going close.

It was a day for important debut goals as Lexi Lloyd-Smith slotted home on her first appearance for Crystal Palace to give the promoted side a priceless 1-0 win against Everton to start their campaign. Another debutant quickly impressed at Tottenham as their new striker Kirsty Hanson scored twice to help them to beat West Ham 3-1.

Liverpool were the day’s most emphatic winners as they cruised to a 4-0 win at promoted Charlton. The Germany striker Vivien Endemann scored on her debut for Liverpool after Grace Fisk had scored twice. Cornelia Kapocs added a stoppage‑time penalty to make it a poor start for Charlton, who did not register a shot on target and recorded just two efforts off target.

Sports.title: European football: Lamine Yamal’s double powers Barcelona to rout of Valencia
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100% start in La Liga.

The reigning champions moved three points clear at the top of La Liga after Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday. Fermín López, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick’s swaggering visitors on a hot afternoon on Spain’s east coast.

Barcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia’s fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium.

“We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team,” said Flick. “We stay calm and then if it’s possible to score we try to do it – it was a fantastic game for us. Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it’s perfect then you can stop working.”

Lamine Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Fermín dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star. Fermín netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after the former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up. Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric García had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with teammate Rodri’s shoulder, on the midfielder’s first start since arriving this summer from Manchester City.

Raphinha, starting again as the team’s centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Fermín fed him. The Valencia goalkeeper, Stole Dimitrievski, saved from Rodri before Pedri netted Barcelona’s fourth after an exchange of passes with Dani Olmo. Gabriel Jesus came on for his Barça debut as a substitute in the final 10 minutes and sent a low effort just wide. Lamine Yamal stayed onside to collect another Olmo pass and put away Barça’s fifth.

Meanwhile, Ronald Koeman Jr, the goalkeeper son of the former Netherlands player and manager Ronald Koeman, scored two penalties for Dutch side Telstar to rescue a point in their Eredivisie match with Cambuur. His second spot-kick was converted in the 11th minute of added time.

Koeman Jr, 31, converted his first penalty on 63 minutes before his ice-cool equaliser. He previously scored from the spot at the end of last season to ensure his side avoided relegation from the Dutch top flight.

View image in fullscreen Telstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr is hugged by a teammate after his late penalty rescued a point. Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock

In Germany, Mainz ignited their Bundesliga season with a thumping 5-0 win over hapless Hamburg, while Augsburg climbed ⁠to the top of the table following a 4-1 win at Eintracht Frankfurt on Sunday.

Mainz took the lead on 19 minutes as Sheraldo Becker was played in on goal by ⁠Kaishu Sano and picked out the bottom corner. Becker then turned provider as his low cross was converted at the back post by Phillipp Mwene for ⁠a 2-0 half-time lead.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Becker was again involved with the next goal as he set up ​Phillip Tietz to bundle the ball home. Tietz ‌then added a fourth ‌as he beat Heuer Fernandes, before Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer punished his former employers ‌with a fifth.

View image in fullscreen Augsburg’s Robin Fellhauer (right) celebrates his goal against Eintracht Frankfurt with teammate Marius Wolf. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

Augsburg have a haul of six points following ​their excellent win at Frankfurt, where they had to come from behind, having trailed 1-0 at half-time. Jonathan Burkardt headed the home side in front inside six minutes.

Arijon Ibrahimovic ​headed in at the back post ​on debut inside the first minute of the re-start for the equaliser. Within a minute, ‌Augsburg were 2-1 ahead ​as the ball ​fell to Robin Fellhauer in the box and he converted to turn the game on its head. Alexis Claude-Maurice and Fabian Rieder added further goals

Augsburg lead the Bundesliga on goal difference ahead of Freiburg, Borussia Dortmund and Elversberg, who all have two wins from two.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy takes party to Burnley after signing deal with Championship strugglers
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy has returned to English football after signing for Burnley in the Championship as a free agent.

Vardy, who will be 40 in January, has signed a contract until the end of the season, having spent last season at Cremonese in Italy. A return to Leicester, where he spent 13 years and was a Premier League champion in 2016 and an FA Cup winner in 2021, was mooted in the summer, only for Vardy to rule out a reunion.

His podcast, Jamie Vardy’s Having A Party, made the news last week for Mike Dean’s lifting of the lid on his antics as a Premier League referee and has secured broadcast rights for a Bundesliga watch-along. He has also, with his wife Rebekah, starred in an ITV reality series, and been the subject of a Netflix documentary.

Despite those wider interests, Vardy’s intention has been to carry on playing, having been a late starter, making his Football League debut at 25 after signing for Leicester.

Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last term and, with Nicky Hayen as their manager, remain without a win after their opening five games of the Championship campaign, losing to Bristol City on Saturday. Vardy joins a team bottom of the division.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town,” Vardy said. “I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”

In June, he said of Leicester, now in League One, currently struggling under the management of Russell Martin: “I think that’s gone. I’ll always support them, always follow them. I think that’s the best thing I can do now.”

Sports.title: Glasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against Spurs
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner argued there was insufficient evidence to disallow Neco Williams’s goal against Tottenham, accusing the video assistant referee Peter Bankes of guessing that the Nottingham Forest defender handled and said ruling it out weakens the officials’ authority. Midway through the second half, Williams stooped to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali attempted to hook the ball clear after Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbled towards the net.

Glasner conceded at least one angle showed Williams appeared to handle the ball, seemingly to protect himself as Tonali went to clear the ball with his left boot, but said the footage was too unclear to disallow the goal. “I don’t think VAR can intervene when he’s guessing,” said Forest’s head coach. “It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention should be very high and this is why it was a wrong intervention for me.

“I’ve watched five or six different angles and to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt [of Williams] moves a little bit, but it’s not clear whether it’s [because of] the ball or Tonali on the goalline. I know refereeing a Premier League game is really difficult – refereeing a training session is sometimes really difficult – but we are told to support the referee, to keep the threshold for VAR intervention very high, to strengthen the referee’s decision and they didn’t do that today. With these kinds of situations, you weaken the referees.”

Bankes checked the goal and then the referee, Craig Pawson, took to the mic before awarding a Spurs free-kick amid a chorus of boos from the home support: “After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest’s No 3 before the goal is scored.” Williams was adamant he did not handle the ball. “I headed it in between my arms,” said the Wales defender, who this week signed a new four-year contract. “If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t. I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms because it never. I knew straight away I’d headed it down in between my arms.”

The disallowed goal was undeniably the moment of an underwhelming contest. For the third successive league match, Tottenham failed to score and this time they did not even muster a shot on target. Dominic Solanke heading on to the roof of the Forest goal, 88 minutes on the clock, was as threatening as they got. Omar Marmoush wellied a shot wide after Spurs countered at speed. Mykhailo Mudryk was brought off the bench for his first competitive minutes for 645 days after a doping suspension but Spurs were blunt. Aside from a 5-1 win against a Charlton B team in the Carabao Cup, their season so far reads: five goals against and none scored.

View image in fullscreen Spurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk came on as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Apart from Gibbs-White’s effort in the buildup to the disallowed goal, Forest’s only other shot on goal was a daisy-cutter from James McAtee. The Spurs league debutant Sávio, a £75m arrival from Manchester City, showed a few neat touches but he and Destiny Udogie were withdrawn after an hour on the advice of Tottenham’s medical department. “I’m not happy when we have the plan but it is for my advantage, my business, the management of the players after their injuries,” said De Zerbi, who accepted his team lacked quality in the final third. “We have to make better decisions, to keep more calm when we are very close to do something important.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

No wonder both teams remain winless. Spurs’s date at home to Everton next weekend has taken on another layer of significance and the same applies to Forest’s trip to Aston Villa. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive in attendance, could be forgiven for wondering when Spurs will see the fruits of their £300m-plus spend, much of the focus on sharpening their attack. They turned to Mudryk, who thrived under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, after the failure to sell Richarlison halted moves for preferred targets Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. This was not the desired result. “We bought very, very good players but you can’t just build the team with the names like in Football Manager,” De Zerbi said.

Sports.title: Gary Neville reveals why he has a 'big fear' about Man United's defence after draw with Everton and names THREE stars at fault for Ainsley Maitland-Niles' stunning 96TH-MINUTE equaliser: 'I was screaming at the TV!'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville reveals why he has a 'big fear' about Man United's defence after draw with Everton and names THREE stars at fault for Ainsley Maitland-Niles' stunning 96TH-MINUTE equaliser: 'I was screaming at the TV!'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gary Neville has torn into Manchester United's defence, admitting he can't see a way out of his former side regularly conceding goals after they shipped two more to Everton on Sunday.

The Red Devils have conceded twice in each of their three Premier League matches so far this season, and they were held to a 2-2 draw with Everton after a last-minute Ainsley Maitland-Niles stunner.

It's an issue manager Michael Carrick is going to have to fix if his side want to be competitive this year – they are currently 11th in the table with one win, one draw and one defeat to their names so far this term.

And Neville has concerns. Questions were raised after the transfer window closed with the club failing to add to their defensive ranks, and the full back-turned pundit is worried it may come back to bite them.

'Manchester United are conceding two goals a game,' he said on the Gary Neville Podcast. 'From a United perspective you can't concede two goals a game, they're on track to concede 76 goals.

'They won't do, but the one thing that I think needed to happen beyond the transfer window with the questions that have been asked about the defence was that Manchester United needed to win today and secondly they couldn't concede goals.

Manchester United shipped two more goals against Everton as they drew 2-2 on Sunday

Gary Neville has admitted he has a 'big fear' that his former side will continue to concede goals

'That last goal is a really bad one. There's a lot that happens before that goal goes in the back of Manchester United's net. When you're playing against a team, it's 2-1, you're away, you've got to push up, you've got to make sure you don't have players sprinting off and doing stupid things.

'Dorgu sprints forward, the ball gets played past him and Everton just drift down that left side so easily. Santos doesn't get across and when he doesn't get across quickly enough Yoro is deep and narrow, almost playing like a third or fourth narrow centre back waiting for the ball to go into the box.

'So they could have stopped it at source. That to me is a real error in the lead-up, and I was screaming as it happened because you know full well you're going to get the ball pumped into the box and you're going to get a team behind desperate in the last few minutes so you have to make sure you're organised and United weren't organised in that last couple of minutes.'

The Red Devils will take on local rivals Manchester City next weekend in the Manchester derby, but first face Azerbaijan side Sabah FK in the Champions League.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez played at centre back against Everton, and it was the same partnership last week in the 5-2 win over Ipswich.

Maguire played with Ayden Heaven on the opening day 2-0 defeat by Hull.

'Teams think they've got a chance against them,' Neville continued. 'I thought they were a little bit complacent and I was saying it after the first goal, they lacked that killer instinct before that period when Everton equalised and then they react again.

'Everton weren't at it at all in that first half – United were the better team and didn't have that killer instinct up top and certainly from 1-0 up to 1-1 they let Everton back in the game. It's not going full throttle when you've got a team down, putting them away and then this liability of conceding goals.

United manager Michael Carrick has expressed his own concerns about the goals they have been conceding

'I don't think it's going to go away and that's my big fear. I think conceding goals is going to chase them and hunt them down the road and I don't know how Michael deals with it because he's got his best back four on the pitch. I don't know why Luke Shaw went off with five minutes to go – hopefully he's not injured. I don't know why Dalot went off with five minutes to go.

'To be fair, Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag used to change their back four a lot as well – you can't be changing your back four. If you've got Hincapie to come on for Calafiori maybe you can, but United have got a back four of Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and Lisandro Martinez and they've not got much behind that. So you can't really change your back four at 1-0 or 2-1.'

Carrick himself was critical of his defence in the wake of the result.

He doesn't have too many options to change things in terms of personnel – with Matthijs De Ligt still missing with a long-term injury. Therefore, Carrick insisted, it's down to his current crop to do better.

'Obviously we can't ignore it,' he said about Maitland-Niles' equaliser. 'We need to concede fewer goals to give us a better chance of winning games. We'll certainly look at that and keep improving.

'There's obviously things we need to get better at as a team. There's been two strikes from distance really, two really good strikes from their point of view. Sometimes they fly in the top corner and more often than not they probably don't.'

Sports.title: Inside Michael Jordan's secret pep talk to inspire his most satisfying championship after bitter legal fight... as familiar face stands in his way
Sports.content:
Inside Michael Jordan's secret pep talk to inspire his most satisfying championship after bitter legal fight... as familiar face stands in his way

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Jordan's last championship came in 1998, but that fierce competitive drive has never left him. And now, less than 12 months after a bitter legal fight, he has a different kind of championship firmly in his sights.

He's waited nearly three decades, so it is no surprise he wants to make this count. Given his six NBA Championships and Finals MVP awards, and his reputation for an unrelenting excellence down the stretch, there is perhaps nobody in sports who could be better placed to pass on pearls of wisdom.

'He's the best guy for it,' Tyler Reddick tells the Daily Mail. This weekend, Reddick begins the NASCAR Chase, the new, 10-race postseason format that will decide the NASCAR Cup Series champion on November 8 at the end of a long, arduous season.

He enters as the third seed and, although teammate Bubba Wallace also made the cut in 14th place, he represents the best hope Jordan has of adding one of his most long-awaited and also most satisfying triumphs.

Less than a year ago, Jordan was traveling from his lakefront North Carolina mansion to Charlotte for a trial at the U.S. District Court. Jordan was ever-present in the courtroom in the Charles R. Jonas Federal Building, giving testimony in a bitter lawsuit as his team and another, Front Row Motorsports, filed an antitrust lawsuit against NASCAR.

After eight long days, on December 11, he stood side by side with NASCAR chairman Jim France after the two sides agreed a settlement and ended their fierce dispute.

Michael Jordan is closing in on a long-awaited championship, this time as a NASCAR owner

Jordan settled a bitter antitrust lawsuit with NASCAR last December in a court in Charlotte

Last month, Jordan instead made the short trip to Airspeed, the state-of-the-art headquarters he built for his race team around 10 miles north of Charlotte in Huntersville, North Carolina.

Instead of needing to win over a jury, he simply had to win over his own employees and deliver some inspiration before their quest for supremacy begins, knowing he is 10 races away from becoming a NASCAR champion team owner.

'For me, anytime I get to spend that time with Michael, it leaves a huge impact on me,' Reddick says. 'I really do love it when he comes to 23XI, to Airspeed, because I have an opportunity to see the impact that he has on the men and women that work here.'

Jordan is far from a passive owner. He regularly attends races, less so when he's vacationing in the summer months, but never misses tuning in wherever he is in the world.

While he tends to keep a low profile at the track, granting the very occasional Fox interview to his trusted reporter, Jamie Little, he is a familiar face these days for the limited number of his employees who travel the country and attend each race.

For the drivers, he is always just a text message away, offering words of congratulations or encouragement after every single race, depending on the result. Sometimes, the text drops before they've even got out of the car.

But every so often, he'll drop in to speak to everyone back at their base, just as he did last month.

Sometimes he gives a heads up, meetings are booked in, the red carpet is rolled out. But often he just stops by, largely unannounced, surprising everyone with his unmissable, 6ft 6inch frame strolling through the front doors.

Tyler Reddick told the Daily Mail about Jordan's recent visit to the 23XI Racing facility

Reddick hopes to drive his No.45 car owned by the NBA legend to a NASCAR Championship

'When he came in here to address the company, he's just a great speaker,' Reddick says. 'He knows how to get the point across, he knows how to get people excited, and he knows how to make it relatable. Just an amazing leader, a great speaker, and for us, it was great that he made the time to come see us, come talk to us.

'Just anytime he makes time for us, it goes a long way.'

At one stage, it all seemed too good to be true for Jordan and Reddick. They won the Daytona 500 - the sport's biggest and first race of the season - in February, then rattled off wins in the next two races. He became the first driver in Cup Series history to win the first three races, with some baseless suggestions even claiming it must be rigged for Jordan's team.

By April 19, Jordan had seen his No.45 car in victory lane five times in the first nine races, the best start to a season since the legendary Dale Earnhardt in 1987. The regular season championship seemed a foregone conclusion, and the top seeding to go with it, bringing a points advantage to start The Chase.

Instead, things started to unfold. Reddick dropped to third in the standings, plagued by just as much bad luck as good luck he had in the first few weeks in a sport where circumstance and fortune are never far away.

It made the timing of Jordan's visit perfect, and Reddick is confident it can help unlock another level of performance, insisting he feels 'really good, honestly,' about where they stand.

'I guess you could look at it one way and say we didn't have a great summer, we dropped from first in the standings to fourth, but the things that were happening in the races for us, like, as catastrophic as they were, for us to not lose more ground, for us to fight through it and still get some amount of points and finish out of those days... it's a really good fight, you know?

'I think everyone wants to go into this Chase and have 10 flawlessly executed races, no mistakes, but...there's gonna be thousands of laps ran. Tens of thousands of decisions to make.

Jordan and Reddick celebrated winning the Daytona 500 in February, NASCAR's biggest race

Jordan was again on hand when Reddick won the third race of the year in a red-hot start

Reddick's team will look to recapture that early season momentum after being inspired by MJ

'People are gonna have mistakes, people are gonna have bad days, and I feel like when they come our way, we've been through just about everything. We know how to handle it, we know how to get through it, we know how to reset for the next week.

'On the other side of it, the majority of the racetracks in The Chase, we've had a lot of speed at, we've won at, we've led laps at, so got a lot of tracks that are strengths for us.

'It's been a really strange way for it to balance itself out, but I think you can look at it one way and say, man, the results really, really went off the edge, just bad, but, within those races, there was many good decisions made, there was a lot of fight, a lot of grit in the team, and trying to dig out of those holes.

'On one hand, it's no fun and not great to have days like that, but for us to push through those days and still make something out of them, was really, really good on our team's part.

'I think for us, yeah, we want to go into this and be as clean as possible, stay out of trouble, have good results, good stage finishes, but again, things are gonna happen.

'It may happen. One driver may go through this whole thing flawlessly, but, it is so hard to do over the course of two and a half months, 10 races. Just being able to stay in it mentally this whole Chase is gonna be super important, and I feel like we had to stretch longer than 10 races where we had just crazy things happened to us, but no one fell out of the fight. We just kept resetting and showing back up the next week, so… in a lot of ways, I feel good about it.'

Reddick has 15 other drivers still hoping to lift the Cup Series Championship at Homestead-Miami Speedway on November 8. But the man to beat, who surpassed him to top the regular season points standings, is Denny Hamlin, Jordan's business partner and co-owner of the team.

While Hamlin is integral to building Reddick's team into a Championship contender, for the next 10 races, he is fully focused on winning his own long-awaited first title at Joe Gibbs Racing as his glittering driving career nears the end.

'I think the battle that was on everyone's mind much of this season is still there,' Reddick admits. 'I think the 11 (Hamlin) will be really strong.'

Joe Gibbs Racing driver Denny Hamlin co-owns 23XI Racing as Jordan's friend and partner

Hamlin and Reddick are fighting one another for the NASCAR Cup Series Championship

But it is clear some of Jordan's mindset has rubbed off on Reddick and his team. They are ready to roll with the punches, focus on themselves and exhibit a mental strength and toughness in line with their boss during his Bulls dynasty.

'I think in a Chase format, your biggest rival, your biggest challenger will be yourself,' Reddick declares. 'It's gonna be really important to stay in it mentally this whole stretch. Again, there's gonna be things that happen, things that don't go according to plan, it's just gonna be super important to stay in it the whole way, mentally.

'We can look at other drivers that will have speed, performance, but, I think it's gonna be important for us to focus on how we maximize each day, and not let the one standout car this week or that week just spin us out with how fast they are. Making the most of each day is gonna be so critical.'

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy returns to England! Striker and wife Rebekah to move back from Italy as he signs surprise deal at Burnley - who are rock bottom of the Championship
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jamie Vardy will be playing his football in England again after signing a contract at Burnley until the end of the season.

The 39-year-old has been a free agent since leaving Italian side Cremonese in the summer following their relegation to Serie B.

Vardy, who moved to Italy with his wife Rebekah and their family, scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 appearances in Serie A last season.

Burnley will be hoping Vardy's experience can help them improve after a poor start to the season – with the Clarets bottom of the Championship after five matches.

They want him to be their No1 striker and his deal has an option for a further year if Burnley are promoted. It is understood he turned down offers from MLS, Serie A and the Premier League.

The scale of his task is clear with the club yet to win a game in the English second tier so far this season – drawing two and losing three of their matches, scoring six and conceding 12 across those matches.

Upon signing for the club, Vardy – who had a Netflix documentary about his career in May – expressed his desire to propel them back up the table.

Jamie Vardy is back in English football after signing a deal at Burnley until end of this season

The move sees Vardy and his wife Rebekah return to England after he played a year in Italy

He scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 Serie A games for Cremonese

He told the club's website: 'I'm really happy to now be here at Burnley.

'This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town.

'I can't wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.'

Burnley head coach Nicky Hayen is excited about what his new striker will add to his struggling squad.

He said: 'We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley.

'His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign. Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt.'

Vardy scored 200 goals in 500 matches for Leicester and won both the Premier League and FA Cup with the club. He is regarded as one of the club's greatest players of all time.

The striker also scored seven goals in 26 appearances for England and was part of the Three Lions squad for Euro 2016 and the 2018 World Cup.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods makes first public appearance since five-year driving ban... as loyalties with Kai Trump torn after Vanessa's public show
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods makes first public appearance since five-year driving ban... as loyalties with Kai Trump torn after Vanessa's public show

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tiger Woods was spotted all smiles on the sidelines at Stanford Stadium on Friday night, making his first public appearance after being hit with a five-year driving ban.

The 15-time major champion returned to his alma mater for the Cardinal's college football clash against the Miami Hurricanes, days after his courtroom appearance.

Sporting a white Stanford cap and a wool quarter zip from his own brand 'Sun Day Red,' Woods was seen laughing and chatting with staffers on the sidelines.

He appeared relaxed and upbeat as he soaked in the action and was also seen in conversation with West Coast rap icon E-40 before the action got underway.

However, the matchup presented an awkward clash of loyalties for the golf legend.

While Woods remains one of Stanford's most celebrated alumni – having won 11 collegiate tournaments before turning pro – his personal ties now run deep in Miami, given his relationship with Vanessa Trump.

Tiger Woods was spotted on the sidelines at Stanford Stadium on Friday night

The 15-time major champion returned to his alma mater for the Cardinal's college football clash

It marked his first public appearance after being hit with a five-year driving ban

Vanessa's 19-year-old daughter, Kai Trump, recently moved to South Florida to begin her freshman year as a collegiate golfer for the University of Miami.

The granddaughter of Donald Trump has regularly documented her move on social media, sharing snaps in Hurricanes gear as she begins her collegiate golf career.

On Friday night, it was Kai's new school that walked away with all the bragging rights, as Miami blew out Woods' beloved Stanford Cardinal in a 45-6 rout.

The outing marked a stark change of scenery from Wednesday morning, when Woods appeared alongside Vanessa to resolve his criminal case stemming from a March 27 crash near his Jupiter Island estate.

Woods' girlfriend held hands with him at the Martin County Courthouse in a show of public solidarity as he finalized his plea deal over a March rollover crash.

Woods pleaded no contest to a reduced charge of reckless driving and refusal to submit to testing, avoiding jail time after entering a plea agreement.

As part of the deal, Woods will have his license suspended for five years.

President Trump declared Woods's plea deal 'very fair' as he weighed in on the matter, just one day after the golf legend discovered his fate from the ordeal.

He added: 'But I think he's going to have somebody drive him. I told him that a long time ago: 'Why don't you get somebody to drive you'

'So he's going to have somebody drive him from now on. He's just a very special guy and I'm glad that was resolved.'

Trump added: 'It's a very tough situation because they didn't find alcohol on him. You know, he didn't test positive at all for alcohol. It's a tough deal when you're taking a painkiller because you're under pain... and you have a problem and you test positive.'

The 15-time major champion was found at the scene of the crash in Jupiter, Florida, with two opioid tablets in his pocket, on March 27.

He has since spent time in rehab in Switzerland but had not been seen publicly since arriving back in America until last month.

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

Sports.title: Goalkeeping son of former Premier League manager scores TWICE to save a draw... but can YOU guess who his famous father is?
Sports.content:
A goalkeeper stepping up to rescue a point for his side by scoring in the 11th minute of added time would be an impressive story in most matches – but to do it with his second goal of the game is simply incredible. Yet that is exactly what happened in the Dutch top tier this weekend, when Telstar’s No1 kept his cool to dispatch two penalties and earn a draw for his 10-man side after going 2-0 down at home to Cambuur. And the goalkeeper’s name will be well known to football fans across the globe – Ronald Koeman Jr is the son of the Netherlands and Barcelona legend and former Southampton and Everton manager. Unsurprisingly, the 31-year-old became the first goalkeeper to score two goals in one Eredivisie game. The drama came after their striker Nokkvi Thorisson saw red for a knee-high challenge in the 22nd minute, leaving the hosts facing playing well over an hour with a man down. Cambuur then took a two-goal lead just after the break before Telstar were awarded a penalty in the 67th minute. Koeman Jr stepped up to bury the ball past Thijs Jansen and halve the deficit. RONALD KOEMAN JR. SCOORT ZIJN TWEEDE VANDAAG EN REDT EEN PUNT 🤯🔥#telcam pic.twitter.com/A3SG3QkHQb — ESPN NL (@ESPNnl) September 6, 2026 Ronald Koeman Jr buries his second spot-kick of the game to earn a 2-2 draw for Telstar The Dutchman has now scored three spot-kicks this year for the Eredivisie side Ronald Koeman, 63, resigned as Netherlands boss after their World Cup exit in the round of 32 A crazy final ten minutes saw Telstar get awarded another penalty, but following a VAR review, referee Joey Kooij reversed his decision to award the spot-kick – only to award another one in the final seconds. He scored his first penalty for Telstar back in May – their final game of last season – after which he revealed he was the club’s first-choice keeper. ‘Back in my youth, I used to take it sometimes and I missed,’ said Koeman Jr after securing a win against FC Volendam. ‘But now I’m shooting it well.’ ‘In the first half of the season, we got two penalties and we missed both of them.
